risk: Research grows without end
mitigation: Risk-driven stop; investigations timeboxed; a budget per subject (METHOD.md section 7)
trigger: a subject passes its budget plus a quarter

risk: The founder is asked too much, or can't follow
mitigation: Only one-way doors go to the founder, each on one page, in plain words; a report at each milestone and planned pause
trigger: a report runs past two pages, or asks more than its one-way decisions

risk: The plan keeps being rewritten
mitigation: METHOD.md changes only by amendment; decisions are superseded, never rewritten
trigger: a change to METHOD.md without an amendment

risk: Agents misread or over-generalize a source
mitigation: Checks scaled by level on the facts decisions rest on; quotes by script; conditions written out; each fact written in its source's own scoped words, and the coordinator's reasoning marked as such (all 15 fixes of D-001's check were in the coordinator's summaries)
trigger: a check finds a fact that says more than its source

risk: Usage limits stop work in flight
mitigation: Small tasks, at most 2 at a time, fresh restarts; the check-in is on only while a task runs
trigger: a task stopped by a limit

risk: A market's facts change (two central banks, sanctions, rates)
mitigation: Each record that depends on a market names its facts and their dates, and a trigger for review
trigger: a newer source contradicts a cited fact

risk: The first market shapes the core
mitigation: The market guard (METHOD.md section 3a), checked by method/decision_status.py --guard
trigger: the guard flags a Built record

risk: Earlier work is lost or redone
mitigation: The baseline is frozen and mapped (METHOD.md section 13); HISTORY.md names every baseline by commit. It failed in execution: section 13's map left out the Q1 concern map, the Shopify payments study, the Yemen setup options and the obligation model, and the changes of 18 and 24 October dropped practices without listing them: the generality rule and the concern-level sweep, then the absence audit and the concern map as the subject index. Proposed, for the founder's go (amendment 4c): each amendment names the risk each retired practice controlled and reassigns it or records it as accepted, and section 13's map gives every body of earlier work a disposition
trigger: work that repeats a held record

risk: The guard becomes ceremony
mitigation: One field per record, and a script; people review only at levels 2 and 3
trigger: guard sections written by rote

risk: Over-correcting drops real constraints, such as cash on delivery or long-pending payments
mitigation: General mechanisms with a precedent are allowed (METHOD.md section 3a)
trigger: a scenario of the first market can't be answered

risk: Scope balloons
mitigation: Only the questions a subject needs, at framing; budgets and stop rules
trigger: a subject's framing lists more decisions than a day holds

risk: Spikes become the product
mitigation: A separate repository, a timebox, and no promotion of their code (METHOD.md section 5)
trigger: spike code proposed for production

risk: Engineering decisions pass by silent veto
mitigation: The veto window starts at the report; level 2 decisions get an independent review
trigger: a report without its engineering decisions listed

risk: Copying Shopify's scale too early
mitigation: A blog is one company's account; prefer options that can grow, with stated triggers
trigger: a decision justified only by another platform's scale

risk: A record fixes a word's meaning without knowing its extent, decides beyond its limits, or rests on another record's or a draft's wording
mitigation: Terms and Scope in every record, checked at its level; the glossary (architecture/12-glossary.md); a record rests on evidence and accepted outcomes only, and names its dependencies (METHOD.md sections 4, 6 and 10; amendment 2); proposed, for the founder's go (amendment 4e): a fact about a platform traces to the platform's own words in the evidence repositories, never to an agent's study, note, draft, model or check sheet, and a script flags records that cite one (D-003's reversal-twin claim came through a chain of agents' notes)
trigger: a record uses a term the glossary lacks, or decides something its Scope leaves open

risk: A message's wording is recorded in place of what it means
mitigation: Each message from the founder is framed first, and the founder can correct the framing; the record holds the framing, not the message (METHOD.md section 3; amendment 2d)
trigger: a decision recorded in the founder's words without its framing

risk: Agent cost estimates leave out that an agent re-reads its whole context at every step, so cost grows with the square of its steps (M1's terms inventory: estimated about 3 million tokens, measured 23.8 million over 106 steps)
mitigation: Each brief caps the agent's steps and asks for small outputs; the cost is measured with method/count_tokens.py after the first 10 steps, and the task is stopped if its projection passes its budget (METHOD.md section 7)
trigger: an agent's measured cost passes its estimate by a quarter

risk: A decision is accepted early, and superseded by a later decision that could have been foreseen
mitigation: The acceptance rule: each item a record leaves open says whether the deciding subject's possible outcomes are carried without changing the record; a record with an item not carried stays proposed or is narrowed (METHOD.md section 6; amendment 3)
trigger: an accepted record superseded by a decision its Scope left open

risk: Checkers agree with a record, or with each other, instead of testing it
mitigation: Each checker's brief asks it to refute each claim against the evidence and to report counter-evidence and missing evidence; the coordinator verifies each finding against its evidence before applying it (METHOD.md section 6; amendment 3); an absence claim names the searches it rests on, across the evidence repositories' structures and not one kind of source (it happened on 24 October: a review's claim from help articles alone was contradicted by Salla's dashboard settings)
trigger: a check that reports only agreement

risk: A decision misses held evidence it never looked for (an omission): a check of its claims can't see it, because it starts from what the record says (choice 2's "never", 25 October; the pilot met the same kind on 13 October, recorded in its method report of 17 October)
mitigation: Proposed, for the founder's go (amendment 4b; reports/M1-method-assessment.md): the checker names the areas a record reaches, receives from method/slice_coverage.py the concern map's concerns there that the record doesn't cite, and says which bear on its claims or on what it leaves open
trigger: a record put for acceptance

risk: The drafts' points say more than their source: about 3 in 10 of those checked; Q5 to Q8 mostly unchecked
mitigation: Each fact a decision rests on is checked at the decision's level (METHOD.md section 6)
trigger: a record cites a draft point

risk: Records leave out a limit their source gives: about 1 in 8 of those checked
mitigation: Conditions written out at levels 2 and 3
trigger: a record rests on a re-frame record

risk: The Knowledge Map's Salla citations point to moved paths (46 of 51), and its pointers date from 8 October
mitigation: Repaired only when a row is used; method/km_select.py marks them
trigger: a subject uses a Salla pointer

risk: The engineering sources were gathered for the payment seam (evidence/shopify-engineering/README.md). By a keyword count of their titles, 17 of the 40 name payments, checkout or a payments team; the rest cover the platform around them, such as pods (E024), modules (E016, E018 to E022), sharding (E015, E023) and peak load (E007, E008). 14 of the 37 web sources are from before 2023 (the README). Corrected on 25 October from "cover payments only", a claim of absence made without a search
mitigation: Each subject adds the outside sources its decisions need (METHOD.md section 5)
trigger: a subject needs outside experience

risk: The Q7 draft keeps the currency table able to hold two rials, against G1's B7
mitigation: The guard, at the markets and currency subject
trigger: S-04 framing

risk: The payment seam's contract v0 puts a currency "edition" on every amount, against G1's B7
mitigation: The guard test in the first subject; done: D-002 removes the edition from the order side, and amounts carry their currency as the foundation defines it (S-04)
trigger: S-01 framing

risk: Decision 1's evidence needs three corrections: the one-way bar between Sana'a and Aden, Stripe's exclusion, and YK-131
mitigation: Corrected before the founder's line (METHOD.md section 14); done: D-001 carries the corrections to YA-62, YA-102, YK-124, YK-131, YK-514 and YK-515
trigger: S-01 framing

risk: The company's country is open (O-01), and a design that assumes one would be hard to undo
mitigation: The constraint that the design assumes no country for the company, and the change scenario with the company in Oman
trigger: S-08, or a decision that names the company's country

risk: These sessions can't push git tags, so baselines have no git names
mitigation: Baselines named by commit in HISTORY.md

risk: The scheduled check-in's old prompt would resume stopped work
mitigation: Turned off on 24 October; its prompt is rewritten to METHOD.md section 9, and it is on only while a task runs
